summary: Configured a routed transit-firewall-pair: node1 (VyOS) fronts node3 on lan-a (10.50.10.0/24), node2 (OPNsense) fronts node4 on lan-b (10.50.20.0/24), routers peer on a transit network (10.50.30.0/24). Both routers default-deny forwarded traffic; a narrow allow was added on each (VyOS forward filter rule + OPNsense pf pass rule) permitting only TCP/8080 from lan-a to node4 (10.50.20.13), plus established/related return traffic. A systemd-managed HTTP service was created on node4:8080 with firewalld opened for that port. Verified node3 reaches node4:8080 via HTTP while ping and other ports between the networks remain blocked in both directions. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all four nodes, confirming changed boot identity and full recovery of addressing, routes, firewall rules, and the HTTP data path after each restart.
actions_performed: Probed L2 adjacency via ARP to discover topology: node1 eth1<->node2 vtnet1 (transit), node1 eth2<->node3 eth1 (lan-a), node2 vtnet2<->node4 eth1 (lan-b)
Configured VyOS (node1): eth1=10.50.30.1/24 (transit), eth2=10.50.10.254/24 (lan-a), static route 10.50.20.0/24 via 10.50.30.2, committed and saved
Configured OPNsense (node2): added opt1=10.50.30.2/24 (transit) and opt2=10.50.20.254/24 (lan-b) interfaces via config.xml, added a gateway item and static route to 10.50.10.0/24 via node1
Configured node3 (10.50.10.12/24) and node4 (10.50.20.13/24) with persistent RHEL7 ifcfg/route files and brought them up via nmcli
Deployed a systemd-managed simplehttp.service on node4 serving on TCP 8080 and opened firewalld port 8080/tcp
Verified default-deny baseline: HTTP and ping both blocked lan-a to lan-b before adding firewall rules
Added VyOS forward filter: default-action drop, rule 5 accepts established/related, rule 10 accepts tcp/8080 from 10.50.10.0/24 to 10.50.20.13 inbound on eth2
Added OPNsense pf pass rule on opt1 (transit ingress) for tcp/8080 from 10.50.10.0/24 to 10.50.20.13; confirmed default block-drop rules remain for everything else
Verified end-to-end: node3 curl to node4:8080 succeeds; ping and port 22 between lan-a and lan-b remain blocked both directions; checked nftables/pf counters as evidence

Captured boot-identity and health baselines on all 4 nodes, then restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 sequentially (one at a time) using native reboot, polled until each came back, and verified changed boot ID plus full recovery of interfaces, routes, firewall rules, and the HTTP service/data path on each
